semantic_contract: 0x00bd8210 is a one-shot direction-key accessor. Given only its receiver, it asks the receiver for a direction through vtable slot +0x58, using a 12-byte stack buffer as the out parameter, then asks the process-wide object at 0x0167eaf8 -- the return value of 0x00b3d350, which the SDK symbol import names Simulator::cGameInputManager::Get -- to turn that three-float direction into a 10-bit index by looking it up in a six-face, 128x128-per-face 16-bit table at receiver+0x4c of that object, rebuilding the table first if the dirty byte at +0x78 is set. The index is returned unchanged. It never writes to the receiver, never writes a global, has no branch, has no error path and takes no argument, so it is a pure query: the only side effects it can trigger belong to 0x00b88590's lazy rebuild. Its callers treat the answer as a comparable identity rather than a magnitude: 0x00d04320 stores the first index it sees and then counts how many further elements return the same value, which is only coherent if the quantisation is stable for equal directions.
classification_rationale: The body, the ABI, the frame arithmetic, the virtual slot offset, both direct callees and the global they dereference are all read directly from the disassembly, and the return semantics are pinned by three inspected call sites in 0x00d04320 that compare the value for equality. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for two named bounds. First, the class that owns 0x00bd8210 is not established: no vtable was located for it, and its only two observed slots (+0x4c and +0x58) match no ModAPI declaration. Second, the class of the object at 0x0167eaf8 is only SDK-name-level evidence: Ghidra carries the imported name Simulator::cGameInputManager::Get on 0x00b3d350, but the ModAPI header for that class declares a 0x114-byte object with no field at +0x4c and none at +0x78, so the layout that 0x00b88590 depends on is observed but not SDK-corroborated. The concrete callee of slot +0x58 is a third, smaller bound. The behaviour itself carries no residual uncertainty.
semantic_findings: 0x00bd8210 is a pure query with no branch, no error path and no write to the receiver; the only side effect available to it is 0x00b88590's lazy table rebuild.
The value it returns is a 10-bit index into a six-face 128x128 16-bit cube table, not a distance, angle or raw coordinate.

The receiver supplies the direction through vtable slot +0x58, which takes a 12-byte out buffer and also returns a pointer to three consecutive floats; the two may or may not be the same object and the evidence does not say.

The quantiser's receiver is a process-wide object reached through 0x00b3d350, so two different receivers compared through 0x00bd8210 share one quantisation table and therefore one index space. That is what makes the equality comparison at 0x00d0441a a meaningful identity test.
0x00b88590 clamps a per-face axis index of 0x80 down to 0x7f, so the +X and -X faces of the cube table each have one unreachable slot; the quantisation is therefore not perfectly uniform.

The receiver is polymorphic but 0x00bd8210 is not: a positive-controlled .rdata/.data dword scan found no vtable entry for it, and 0x00d04320 calls it directly after loading the receiver from an array element.
unresolved_questions: The binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so no class identity can be read from typeinfo; class claims in this record rest only on observed vtable data and SDK header text.
No original-process trace exists for any function in this batch. Every statement here is static.
What class owns 0x00bd8210? Its slot +0x4c is used at 0x00d043cf in the same caller but matches no ModAPI declaration, and no vtable for it was located.

Is the object at 0x0167eaf8 really a cGameInputManager? The SDK import names 0x00b3d350 as Simulator::cGameInputManager::Get, but the ModAPI header for that class declares neither the +0x4c table nor the +0x78 dirty byte, so the name may be right while the layout is a different class reached through the same accessor.

What does the 12-byte out buffer at 0x00bd8218 receive, and is it the same memory as the three floats that 0x00b88590 reads? The slot's return value and its out parameter are separate and the body uses only the return value.

What are the 10 bits at 0x00b8875a? They index a 6*128*128*2-byte table, so they are a packed face/u/v code or a precomputed lighting, navigation or animation index. No writer of that table was located.
Is 0x00b87dc0 a full rebuild of the table or an incremental update? Only the call site was read.
Eleven of the fourteen observed call sites in region 0x00bf0000 were not disassembled, so their use of the return value is unverified.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00bd8210, so the claim that equal directions always quantise to equal indices is static-only.
The 12-byte out buffer written by the slot +0x58 callee must be observed in a live process before its role can be named.
A runtime check must confirm whether the table at receiver+0x4c is rebuilt (dirty byte +0x78) at the moments 0x00bd8210 runs, since that is the only side effect on the path.
